# dlarft

> Forms the triangular factor T of a real block reflector H of order N.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dlarft from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dlarft';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dlarft( order, direct, storev, N, K, V, LDV, TAU, strideTAU, T, LDT ) → Float64Array
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | in |  | one of `'row-major'`, `'column-major'` | storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `direct` | `("forward"\|"backward")` | in |  |  | `'forward'` or `'backward'` |
| `storev` | `("columnwise"\|"rowwise")` | in |  |  | `'columnwise'` or `'rowwise'` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | order of the block reflector |
| `K` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | number of elementary reflectors |
| `V` | `Float64Array` | in | `N × K` |  | input matrix |
| ↳ `LDV` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  |  | leading dimension of `V` |
| `TAU` | `Float64Array` | in | `K` |  | input array |
| ↳ `strideTAU` | `integer` | in |  |  | `TAU` stride length |
| `T` | `Float64Array` | out | `K × K` |  | input matrix |
| ↳ `LDT` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  |  | leading dimension of `T` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `direct`: Specifies the order in which the elementary reflectors are multiplied to form the block reflector:

  -   `= 'F'`: $H = H(1)$ H(2) . . . H(k) (Forward)
  -   `= 'B'`: $H = H(k)$ . . . H(2) H(1) (Backward)
- `storev`: Specifies how the vectors which define the elementary reflectors are stored (see also Further Details):

  -   `= 'C'`: columnwise
  -   `= 'R'`: rowwise
- `N`: The order of the block reflector H. $N \ge 0$.
- `K`: The order of the triangular factor T (= the number of elementary reflectors). $K \ge 1$.
- `V`: (`LDV`,N) if `STOREV = 'R'` The matrix V. See further details.
- `TAU`: `TAU(i)` must contain the scalar factor of the elementary reflector H(i).
- `T`: The k by k triangular factor T of the block reflector. If `DIRECT = 'F'`, T is upper triangular; if `DIRECT = 'B'`, T is lower triangular. The rest of the array is not used.

</details>

**Returns** `Float64Array`: `T`

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "forward", "backward"
- `TypeError` third argument must be one of the following: "columnwise", "rowwise"

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dlarft.ndarray(
    direct, storev,
    N, K,
    V, strideV1, strideV2, offsetV,
    TAU, strideTAU, offsetTAU,
    T, strideT1, strideT2, offsetT
) → Float64Array
```

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `direct` | `("forward"\|"backward")` | in |  |  | `'forward'` or `'backward'` |
| `storev` | `("columnwise"\|"rowwise")` | in |  |  | `'columnwise'` or `'rowwise'` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | order of the block reflector |
| `K` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | number of elementary reflectors |
| `V` | `Float64Array` | in | `N × K` |  | matrix of reflector vectors |
| ↳ `strideV1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of first dim of V |
| ↳ `strideV2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of second dim of V |
| ↳ `offsetV` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for V |
| `TAU` | `Float64Array` | in | `K` |  | array of scalar factors |
| ↳ `strideTAU` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for TAU |
| ↳ `offsetTAU` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for TAU |
| `T` | `Float64Array` | out | `K × K` |  | output triangular matrix |
| ↳ `strideT1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of first dim of T |
| ↳ `strideT2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of second dim of T |
| ↳ `offsetT` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for T |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `direct`: Specifies the order in which the elementary reflectors are multiplied to form the block reflector:

  -   `= 'F'`: $H = H(1)$ H(2) . . . H(k) (Forward)
  -   `= 'B'`: $H = H(k)$ . . . H(2) H(1) (Backward)
- `storev`: Specifies how the vectors which define the elementary reflectors are stored (see also Further Details):

  -   `= 'C'`: columnwise
  -   `= 'R'`: rowwise
- `N`: The order of the block reflector H. $N \ge 0$.
- `K`: The order of the triangular factor T (= the number of elementary reflectors). $K \ge 1$.
- `V`: (`LDV`,N) if `STOREV = 'R'` The matrix V. See further details.
- `TAU`: `TAU(i)` must contain the scalar factor of the elementary reflector H(i).
- `T`: The k by k triangular factor T of the block reflector. If `DIRECT = 'F'`, T is upper triangular; if `DIRECT = 'B'`, T is lower triangular. The rest of the array is not used.

</details>

**Returns** `Float64Array`: `T`

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "forward", "backward"
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "columnwise", "rowwise"
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer

</section>

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import discreteUniform from '@stdlib/random/array/discrete-uniform/lib/index.js';
import dlarft from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dlarft';

/** @type {{ dtype: 'float64' }} */
const opts = {
	'dtype': 'float64'
};
const N = 3;
const V = discreteUniform( N * N, -10, 10, opts );
const T = discreteUniform( N * N, -10, 10, opts );
const TAU = discreteUniform( N, -10, 10, opts );

// Using the standard interface:
let out = dlarft( 'row-major', 'forward', 'columnwise', N, N, V, N, TAU, 1, T, N );
console.log( out );

// Using the ndarray interface:
out = dlarft.ndarray( 'forward', 'columnwise', N, N, V, N, 1, 0, TAU, 1, 0, T, N, 1, 0 );
console.log( out );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DLARFT`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DLARFT forms the triangular factor T of a real block reflector H of order n, which is defined as a product of k elementary reflectors.

If `DIRECT = 'F'`, $H = H(1)$ H(2) . . . H(k) and T is upper triangular;

If `DIRECT = 'B'`, $H = H(k)$ . . . H(2) H(1) and T is lower triangular.

If `STOREV = 'C'`, the vector which defines the elementary reflector H(i) is stored in the i-th column of the array V, and

$$
H = I - V \, T \, V^T
$$

If `STOREV = 'R'`, the vector which defines the elementary reflector H(i) is stored in the i-th row of the array V, and

$$
H = I - V^T \, T \, V
$$

### Further Details

The shape of the matrix V and the storage of the vectors which define the H(i) is best illustrated by the following example with $n = 5$ and $k = 3$. The elements equal to 1 are not stored.

`DIRECT = 'F'` and `STOREV = 'C'`: `DIRECT = 'F'` and `STOREV = 'R'`:

$$
V = \begin{pmatrix} 1 &  &  \\ v_{1} & 1 &  \\ v_{1} & v_{2} & 1 \\ v_{1} & v_{2} & v_{3} \\ v_{1} & v_{2} & v_{3} \end{pmatrix} V = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & v_{1} & v_{1} & v_{1} & v_{1} \\  & 1 & v_{2} & v_{2} & v_{2} \\  &  & 1 & v_{3} & v_{3} \end{pmatrix}
$$

`DIRECT = 'B'` and `STOREV = 'C'`: `DIRECT = 'B'` and `STOREV = 'R'`:

$$
V = \begin{pmatrix} v_{1} & v_{2} & v_{3} \\ v_{1} & v_{2} & v_{3} \\ 1 & v_{2} & v_{3} \\  & 1 & v_{3} \\  &  & 1 \end{pmatrix} V = \begin{pmatrix} v_{1} & v_{1} & 1 &  &  \\ v_{2} & v_{2} & v_{2} & 1 &  \\ v_{3} & v_{3} & v_{3} & v_{3} & 1 \end{pmatrix}
$$

</section>
